title: Running Headers (Page Information Line) -- Good Practice Description

illustrates.quote: Guiding principles: Each braille page should generally carry a page information line (PIL) indicating the braille page number, the print page number (optional), and title or current section name. It should be easily located by the reader.

blocks.features: Prose description of the recommended page-information-line layout: print page number left-justified, title/section name centred, braille page number right-justified, all on one line, title summarised (not truncated), capitals optional. The worked example follows separately (b004-6-2). No print/braille pair given here.

print.surroundingText: Followed by an N.B. that most braille translation software can auto-generate this header (though not shorten titles).

braille.notes: No worked braille given in this item; it is the prose statement of good practice. See b004-6-2 for the worked example.

resolution: Both runs agree: prose-only, no braille. status: no-braille.
